question.prompt: Joe had walked half way from home to school when he realized he was late. He ran the rest of the way to school. He ran \(3\) times as fast as he walked. Joe took \(6\) minutes to walk half way to school. How many minutes did it take Joe to get from home to school?

solutions.explanation:
Joe walks half the journey and runs the other half, so the two distances are equal. Covering the same distance at three times the speed takes one-third as much time. His running time is therefore
\[
6\div3=2\text{ minutes}.
\]
Adding the walking and running times gives \(6+2=\boxed{8}\) minutes, choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Compare times for equal distances
